title: Chemistry helps flag stability disagreements in GNoME materials
summary: Within a selected subset of GNoME materials, a fitted ranking using composition and hull distance found 45.8% of the cases where two density functional workflows disagreed, compared with 40.4% for hull distance alone. Both figures use a 20% screening budget across held-out prototype-cluster splits. Either workflow’s verdict can differ from experimental stability.

source_review.scope: arXiv v1 front matter, data provenance, Sections 3 and 4.12 and limitations

evidence.tested: The ranking comparison used 117,018 records initially labeled stable with 7,822 structural-prototype proxy clusters, repeated over 20 cluster splits. The target was a precomputed change in stability verdict.
evidence.unknown: The sample was selected for available recomputations. Relative ranking varied with chemistry and reference construction. Actual thermodynamic stability and out-of-catalog performance were untested.
evidence.ai_role: The audited population comes from GNoME candidate discovery. Fitted logistic regression used chemistry-cell disagreement rates and distance to the reference hull to rank candidates for review.
